correctness.rationale: For a transitive three-candidate majority tournament both objectives choose the topological order. For a directed 3-cycle, Slater's three optimal orders each reverse one majority edge, whereas Kemeny minimizes the reversed majority-margin weight, so its top set is obtained from the weakest cycle edge or tied weakest edges. Every three-voter majority cycle has margins \((1,1,1)\), while the five-voter witness \(2ABC,2BCA,1CAB\) has margins \((1,3,1)\). A fresh independent exact replay of all labeled profiles for electorate sizes \(1,3,5\) reproduced the histograms \(6\); \(204+12\); and \(7236+360+180\), and an independent anonymous replay found exactly six divergent profiles with multinomial weight \(180\). The frozen verifier source was also read; its finite exhaustions corroborate the structural proof.
correctness.risk: The universal lower boundary is proved only for exactly three candidates and odd strict-ballot electorates.

value.rationale: This is a natural first-divergence boundary between two classical aggregation rules, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It gives the complete smallest odd-electorate classification, prevalence, margin geometry and symmetry orbit after the local three-candidate rule behavior is known.
value.risk: The result does not provide a frequency formula for larger electorates or more candidates.

final_claim: For three candidates with complete strict ballots and an odd electorate, Kemeny and Slater have identical top-candidate sets for one and three voters; five voters are the first possible divergence. Exactly \(180\) of the \(6^5=7776\) labeled five-voter profiles diverge, all with cyclic majority-margin multiset \((1,1,3)\), forming one anonymous candidate-relabeling orbit and giving probability \(5/216\).
limitations: Exactly three candidates, strict complete ballots and odd electorates.
The complete frequency statement is only for the first divergent electorate size.
